plainTranslation: Directly opposing drives. You want the same intensity aimed in opposite directions - magnetic and exhausting. Failure mode: every difference becomes a contest. Take turns leading, agree on direction first, and stop treating the relationship as a fight to win.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Imported from approved project marquee synastry aspect material. Source file was not copied into the repository.
summaryDeep:
You and this person may push in very different ways. One of you wants to act now. The other wants to wait. One of you charges directly at the problem. The other holds position, studies the room, or refuses to be moved before they are ready.

This can be compelling because the other person has something you may not naturally use. Their boldness may pull you forward. Their patience may slow you down in a way you need. Their way of handling pressure may frustrate you, but it can also show you another kind of strength.

When this works, the two of you cover more ground together. One person brings momentum. The other brings timing. One person pushes the door open. The other makes sure it is the right door. The difference can become strategy instead of conflict.

This difference can carry into the physical side too. Mars is the body as much as the will, and here desire often runs on a little tension. One of you may move faster than the other, want when the other is holding back, or chase a rhythm the other does not quite share. That gap can be charged in a good way, but it asks you to find a pace that actually works for both bodies rather than assuming one speed fits.

The harder part is that ordinary decisions can turn into a tug of war. You want to go one way, they want to go another. You want movement, they want control. They may feel rushed by you, while you may feel blocked by them. Before long, the issue is no longer the plan. It is who gets to decide the pace.

Do not make the other person's way of acting into the enemy. Decide what you are trying to accomplish first. Once you know the goal, the two different approaches can work together instead of pulling the relationship apart.
